knowledge_point.title: Expressing a Vector That Satisfies a Ratio in Terms of Known Vectors

question.:question/problem:
![](images/fe/fe6706b73465189953747609b4361117a28e88a566f0693dcef884ba70a4f5cb.png)

Consider the diagram above, where $\overset{\to }{OA}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{OB}=b$ and $T$ divides $\overset{―}{AB}$ in the ratio $AT:TB=4:1.$ Express $\overset{\to }{OT}$ via the vectors $a$ and $b$.

$\,\overset{\to }{OT}=$
{{field-1}}
$a+$
{{field-2}}
$b$
question.:question/worked-solution:
From the diagram, we see that

$$
\overset{\to }{OT}=\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AT}.
$$

We're told that $\overset{\to }{OA}=a,$ so we just need to work out $\overset{\to }{AT}.$

First, from $△OAB,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =\overset{\to }{AO}+\overset{\to }{OB} \\  & =-\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{OB} \\  & =-a+b \\  & =b-a.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $AT:TB=4:1,$ we have

$$
\overset{\to }{AT}=\frac{4}{5}\overset{\to }{AB}=\frac{4}{5}(b-a).
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OT} & =\overset{\to }{OA}+\overset{\to }{AT} \\  & =a+\frac{4}{5}(b-a) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}a+\frac{4}{5}b.\end{aligned}
$$
